name: Stouffville–Toronto
description: The Stouffville corridor’s Union-bound bus family, historically extending to Uxbridge. Short workings, station bypasses and express variants changed with rail service, with route 70 providing many northern train connections.

timeline.event: The recovered timetable documents Uxbridge–Goodwood–Stouffville–Markham–Union bus trips and shorter train-connecting trips.
Lincolnville is included in the original Stouffville timetable, replacing the earlier north-Stouffville street timing point for relevant services.
Routes 70 and 71 share the timetable; the 71 family includes multiple Union-bound and short variants.
Lincolnville GO was renamed Old Elm GO.
Buses and trains began serving the relocated Old Elm station.

sources.title: GO Stouffville Table 71, printed effective December 30, 2006; archive filename March 3, 2008

Town of Whitchurch-Stouffville 2021 Year in Review: Lincolnville renamed October 16, 2021
GO relocates Old Elm station, October 17, 2023 — Transit Toronto

gaps: The 2006 table contains several express and short-working combinations without sufficiently clear public suffixes; only the explicitly supported patterns are diagrammed.
Earlier Uxbridge services to Scarborough Centre or downtown Toronto require separate historical timetables before assigning them a modern route number.
These are documented dated snapshots. Changes between snapshots, temporary diversions and every historical local stop have not all been recovered.

GTFS dates identify captured feeds, not necessarily the first or last day of a route. Open a pattern to see its exact scheduled service dates. Temporary rail replacement and special-service patterns are included when present in the source.
Manually reconstructed versions generally contain published timetable timing points / major stops. They must not be read as complete roadside stop inventories.
